title: Implement Custom 'myInstanceOf' Operator
problemStatement: Implement `myInstanceOf(instance, Constructor)` that mimics the native `instanceof` operator by walking `instance`'s prototype chain checking for `Constructor.prototype`.
interviewTrap: Primitives (`myInstanceOf('string', String)`) return false because `instanceof` only checks object instances, not primitive values.

testCases.name: Walks up multiple prototype inheritance tiers

details.name: Walks up multiple prototype inheritance tiers

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Every JS object has an internal `[[Prototype]]` link. Property lookup walks this chain until the property is found or `null` is reached (`Object.prototype.__proto__ === null`). Modifying a property on an instance creates an 'own property' shadowing the prototype's property.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for ECMAScript instanceof Algorithm & Prototype Comparison.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), ECMAScript instanceof Algorithm & Prototype Comparison is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Primitives (`myInstanceOf('string', String)`) return false because `instanceof` only checks object instances, not primitive values.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does the 'instanceof' operator actually work according to the specification?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Per ECMA-262 §13.10.2, `a instanceof B` evaluates `B[Symbol.hasInstance](a)`. The default `Symbol.hasInstance` implementation extracts `B.prototype` and walks the prototype chain of `a`: `let proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(a)`. It loops: if `proto === B.prototype`, return `true`; if `proto === null`, return `false`; else `proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(proto)`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of the underlying Symbol.hasInstance algorithm.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does 'instanceof' fail across iframe or worker boundaries?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Each iframe or window context has its own distinct execution realm with its own distinct built-in constructors (`windowA.Array !== windowB.Array`). An array created in iframe B has `Object.getPrototypeOf(arr) === windowB.Array.prototype`. Checking `arr instanceof windowA.Array` returns `false`! This is why `Array.isArray()` was introduced to check identity across realms.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The classic multi-realm / iframe trap question.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Can an object customize its own instanceof behavior?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Yes! Any class or constructor can define a static `[Symbol.hasInstance](instance)` method to override the default prototype walking behavior and implement custom type checking logic.

realWorldUseCases.description: Checking whether an object received from an iframe, foreign realm, or worker is an Array using internal slot checks rather than instanceof.
Creating duck-typing classes where `instanceof` checks for specific interface methods rather than prototype links.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: class IterableType { static [Symbol.hasInstance](x) { return x != null && typeof x[Symbol.iterator] === 'function'; } }

howToExplain.opening: The instanceof operator is not a class check; it is a prototype chain equality walk that tests whether a constructor's .prototype exists anywhere in an instance's prototype chain.
keyPoints: instanceof executes Symbol.hasInstance on the right-hand constructor.
Walks the prototype chain of the left operand using Object.getPrototypeOf.
Fails across different iframes/realms because each realm has independent constructor identities.
Symbol.hasInstance allows custom runtime type checks.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Knowing that instanceof is just prototype walking explains why it fails across iframes and why Array.isArray is necessary.
analogies: Checking someone's lineage: you walk up their family tree parent by parent to see if a specific ancestor's name appears.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using instanceof to check primitive strings or numbers.
commonMistakes.why: 'hello' instanceof String returns false because primitives are not objects and do not have prototype chain wrappers until boxed.
commonMistakes.correct: Use typeof for primitives or Object(val) instanceof String.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does Array.isArray verify an array across realms without prototype walking?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Per ECMA-262 §23.1.2.1, `Array.isArray` inspects the internal `[[Class]]` / `[[ArrayData]]` slot of the object. If the object is an exotic Array object, it returns true regardless of which realm or prototype it belongs to.
